notes: none by day; two bandits shake down late travellers after dark

skirmisher bandits in the stair-hall, a caster on the fallen parapet. The caster is the one Hush-speaking hand the Hearthvale bandits have: a Spire dropout, the smuggler-Sayer, gone inland. Five of them, as A Verse About You counts them: the Larkbourne Boys keep hall here.

a pack of bandits with a brute leader. Ryn Larkbourne leads the band in talk, and the Roll of Names sends you to hear Ryn out; the brute who leads it in a fight is the Larkbourne Bruiser, at the fire with the pack. While the errand is to hear Ryn, the band keeps its hands off its knives.

safe ground; a place to lure barrow-wights and watch them turn away. The barrow's nearest dead work the hedges two hundred metres off and are leashed to them, so two come up the hedge line past the gravestones after dark and stop there; the yew's ground (its POI def's ward) is ground the dead will not cross, and a wight whose quarry stands under it turns for home.
a down-wolf pack in the cave behind the falls: the dark mouth at the foot of the face, behind the water
bristlebacks rooting in the dell at dawn

cutpurses work the toll queue; a bravo duels anyone who refuses to pay. The guilds' bravo keeps the toll table by day and asks five marks of whoever touches it; whoever walks on past the table without paying has it out with him. The cutpurses work the queue on the landward approach.
smugglers with a dropout Sayer casting Hush
gutter drakes in the hull
leech-hounds come up the channel at night
bog-drowned climb the poles after dark if the lanterns are out: while Lissane is walking her round they are lit.
wisps circle at midnight

sallowjaw ambush from the water inside the ring; a moral choice with reputation cost. They lie in the pool under the King's roots and come up at whoever walks into the ring; the reedfolk feed them so they nest nowhere else, and the Reed Council hears of every one the player kills here. Walking back out of the ring costs nothing.

killing_costs.notice: The reedfolk feed the Sallow King's sallowjaws so they nest nowhere else. The Reed Council will hear who killed one.

notes: leech-hounds in the hold; a chart of the Salt Isles, on the crate under her bow

none; a book and a side quest. The book is the hermit's own exercise book from his clerking years, the name on its flyleaf boxed out, read on his crate where he leaves it; the side quest is his (npcs/poi_people.json, quests/side_2.json).
bog-drowned rise from between the columns as you pass
wisps lure toward deep water

sentinels: do not fight them unless you are carrying stolen forest goods. A Warden at each end of the arch lets anyone cross who carries nothing they did not need, and wakes for anyone who comes within its reach carrying what was taken out of the Briarwold (a Warden's own heartwood, a Hart-Knight's antler or crown or spear, weaver silk, the moss and the fungus off the old trees) or who takes something within its reach.
skirmisher archers above
weaver ambush from above at night; safe by day. They wait on the shelf of the lip beside the fall.
a Hart-Knight keeps vigil at the skull
ash-wights (swarm) far from home: the four the Briar's Purpose sends you to put down are these
weavers on the bridges
crag-wolves on the far approach at night (the toll-keeper is a person: npcs/poi_people.json)
crag-wolf pack in the skull
scree-hags on the cliffs above shriek at climbers: on the top ledge, over all three falls
elite raiders in heavy plate; a brute and two skirmishers: the Clanless Hewer, who goes in first in the heaviest plate, and two Outriders in plate cut down to run, who go wide.
scree-hags on the scree
ash-wights under the arch

choristers around the excavation. By day it is the Sayers' dig (the story: 'A Sayer camp digs here and argues'); after dark the choristers come and stand round it and hold the note at it, which is what the knight in the Headless Watch warns you of.
swarm; they only rise if you touch the cup

a fallen Tolling knight on the stair if the watch has turned; otherwise a friendly vigil. The watch has turned while the Order's fallen are standing the north walk: from the Names in the Chapter Book's walk out to it until the book is answered. Otherwise only Calen Ash keeps the eye.
a bell-bearer at the top rings when it sees you: on the shelf of the lip, beside the glass
the tutorial: ash-wights on the stair
The Hart of Thorns keeps the circle. Its arena was always the Moot; nothing stood it up there, so the main thread's fourth account could not be finished.
